answer.evidence: The main body is a sign board on a thin pole (rows 0-14 at width 10, pole rows 15-27 at width 4). The board is drawn face-on. Its pale top rows 1-3 are part of the painted sign face, with no front-edge line or eave shadow, and the width profile has no ellipse. The base (rows 28-31, widths 6 then 8) has only a 1-row highlight at row 29, which is a rim at most and not a top surface. The whole object is a flat front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin pole-mounted sign with a small head and a base. By the numbers it has 13 visible tones per tile, against 6 for bus-shelter, 12 for kiosk and 20 for vending. Near-flat coverage is 0%, and the dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted rather than black. Judged by eye, the sign head has a light/mid/dark ramp with a dark bluish-navy edge, and the pole and base are shaded with a highlight, so it reads as the same family as the references. It is sparse and sits at the low end of the shading-step range, but it is not thinner or more sticker-like than the shipped bus-shelter and kiosk. A careful artist would accept it next to them.

It has no front-edge line or eave shadow below it, and the width stays at 10 from row 1 to row 14. The pole (rows 15-27, width 4) is a plain vertical shaft. The base (rows 28-31, widths 6-8) has a lighter row 29 and a darker row 30 between outline rows, which reads as a 1-row rim at most, not a top surface. Nothing widens and then narrows to form an ellipse, and no roof, contents or side face is visible. The whole object is a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin pole sign with a small sign head and a round base. Its measured facts are 13 visible tones per tile, 0% near-flat coverage and 0% neutral dark edge pixels. That is at or above bus-shelter-a (6) and kiosk-a (12), and below vending-a (20). The outline pixels carry a tint, not neutral black, so they read as dark material tone like the references. The sign head shows a lit face, a darker frame, and a small number glyph/lamp with highlight and shade, and the pole and base have a light-to-dark ramp. Shading is a bit shallower than the larger references, but that is expected for a thin object, and it would not look thinner or flatter beside them. No large flat fills.
